turns.t: Hello, doctor. I'm not sure what I've come about, to be honest. The hospital said to come back and see you after I was in.
Yes, you were in for a chest infection three weeks ago. How have you been since you came home? ~
Grand, grand. Only I've no appetite. None at all. I push the food around the plate.
How long has that been going on?
Since the hospital? Or before it? Honestly, I couldn't say. I've been off my food a while.
Have you lost weight?
My trousers are loose, so I must have. A couple of stone, maybe? I don't weigh myself.
Do you feel sick, or does food stick, or does it hurt to eat? ~
No, none of that. I'm just not hungry. ~
What tablets are you on?
Mirtazapine, 15 mg, maybe? At bedtime, the little white one. And omeprazole, 20 mg in the morning.
Is the mirtazapine 15 mg, do you think? You said maybe.
It could be 30. The chemist knows. I only take what they give me.
I'll check with the record. What's it for? ~
For my mood, after my wife died. Two years ago.
I'm very sorry. Any operations?
Gallbladder, in the nineties.
Let me weigh you, and check your numbers. ~
Go on then. ~
Pulse 82, blood pressure 118 over 72, temperature 36.6, oxygen 96 percent, and you weigh 64 kilos.
Is that a lot? ~
Your record says 74 kilos a year ago, so you've lost about ten kilos, which is significant. Any cough or breathlessness left from the chest infection?
A little cough in the morning. No breathlessness.
I'd say the main thing is poor appetite after your recent illness, in the setting of low mood, so I'd call it reduced appetite following illness.
Do you think it's my mood? ~
It's likely part of it, but with that much weight loss, I don't want to assume. I'd like to arrange blood tests, to look for anaemia, thyroid, and other causes.
Right. ~
Meanwhile, small meals and snacks, six times a day, and a build-up drink between meals, rather than big plates.
I could manage a milky drink. ~
That's the idea. And try to eat with someone, if you can, a neighbour or a friend.
My daughter comes on Sundays. ~
Good. I'd like to see you again in two weeks, and weigh you again.
Two weeks. Fine. Thank you, doctor. ~
